name: 174. A fallback that served a request with a direct key does not become the session's provider (session-direct-key)
description:
A direct key (x-bf-direct-key: true plus the caller's own provider key, enabled by client.allow_direct_keys) is tried only on the first route of the chain; fallbacks run on the gateway's keys. A fallback that served such a request used to become the session's provider, so the next request of the session was moved there first and the caller's key was sent to a provider it was never meant for. That attempt was refused, and the demoted provider then served on the gateway's keys. A fallback that serves a direct-key request now binds no route, and the next request follows the routing decision.

The row builds two run-scoped OpenAI-backed providers, each with a working gateway key, and a header-gated rule targeting P1 with P2 as its fallback. Turn 1 sends a throwaway direct key on a session: P1 refuses it and P2 serves as the fallback. Turn 2 repeats it on the same session and must start on P1 again: P1 refuses the key and P2 serves as the fallback, with the request's primary attempt logged on P1. Before the change turn 2 started on P2 and P1 served it as the fallback. Everything is deleted by the row. Run with FEATURE="session-direct-key".

item.name: openai session with a direct key starts on the routed provider again after a fallback served - session-direct-key
